title: Retrieving Intent-covering Demonstrations for Clarification Generation in Conversational Search Systems

problem.claim: Clarification facet generation for ambiguous or multi-facet queries must support disambiguation and user interaction in open-domain conversational Web search.

gap.claim: Existing demonstration-selection methods predominantly rely on query similarity and fail to account for the multi-dimensional nature of query intents, which can produce facets misaligned with user needs.

contributions.claim: An intent-covering framework selects demonstrations that comprehensively cover the diverse intents underlying a query.
A generative model with beam search predicts potential intents, and an intent-document graph captures their semantic relationships.
A heuristic greedy algorithm maximizes intent coverage for demonstration selection, while a re-ranking model optimizes demonstration order for contextual alignment.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments report superiority over strong baselines across various lexical and semantic evaluation metrics.
An in-depth analysis examines how the number, order, and contextual relevance of demonstrations influence generation performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Search clarification supports disambiguation and interaction in open-domain conversational Web search.
In-context learning uses static or similarity-based demonstrations for facet generation.
Query-similarity-based methods overlook multi-dimensional query intents and may generate misaligned facets.
The framework predicts intents, models intent-document relationships, selects intent-covering demonstrations, and reranks their order.
Experiments compare the approach with strong baselines and analyze demonstration factors affecting performance.

source_observation.claim: Demonstration selection is optimized for coverage of diverse query intents rather than query similarity alone.

interpretation.claim: Prompt examples may be more effective when they represent the relevant dimensions of a user's intent space.

application.claim: For clarification or facet-generation systems, select and order demonstrations using predicted intent coverage and contextual alignment.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether intent coverage improves performance across domains, query types, or deployment conditions beyond the reported evaluations.

source_observation.claim: The reported analysis varies the number, order, and contextual relevance of demonstrations.

interpretation.claim: Prompt construction factors can materially affect generated clarification quality.

application.claim: Evaluate demonstration-based prompting with controlled variation of example count, ordering, and relevance.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the analysis protocol, effect sizes, or which factors were most influential.

unknowns: Datasets, query domains, and experimental settings are unspecified.
The intent-prediction model, graph construction, greedy objective, and reranking architecture are unspecified.
Baseline identities, metric values, statistical testing, and ablation results are unspecified.
